concepts.title: Mean as the Balance Centre
concepts.definition: The arithmetic mean is the balance point of a data set: it equals the sum of all values divided by how many there are, and the total distance of the values below it equals the total distance of the values above it - not the midpoint of the extremes, but the levelling point of the whole set.
concepts.key_idea: Average of 3 and 7 is 5, exactly where the extra of one fills the gap of the other.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp205.txt lines 1-80 (balancing act, dot plots, equal distances)
question_patterns: find the mean of 3 and 7 and show it is the balance point

solution_steps.explain: The total is the sum of every value in the data.

solution_steps.action: divide by the number of values
solution_steps.explain: Sharing the total equally gives the mean.

concepts.title: Finding a Missing Value from the Mean
concepts.definition: When one data value is lost but the mean and all other values are known, the total can be rebuilt as mean times count, and subtracting the known values leaves the missing one - the coach's smudged wrestler weight works out as 392 minus 349, or 43 kg.
concepts.key_idea: Rebuild the total first: mean x count, then take away what is already known.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp205.txt lines 105-160 (finding the unknown, wrestlers 39.2 kg mean)
question_patterns: the mean weight of 10 wrestlers is 39.2 kg and nine weights are known - find the smudged weight
a value is unreadable in the data - recover it from the mean
find the missing entry when the average and the other values are given
why does mean times count give the sum of all values
the mean of five numbers is 20 and four of them are known - find the fifth
check the recovered value by recomputing the mean

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the mean by the number of values.
Whatever remains belongs to the missing entry.

concepts.title: Correcting the Mean After an Error
concepts.definition: If one recorded value turns out wrong by a known amount, first undo it on the total - multiply the old mean by the count, adjust by the error, then divide again - as when one tree's coconut count was 3 too many and the true average fell from 25.6 to 25.4.
concepts.key_idea: One wrong entry shifts the total by the size of the error, and the mean follows.
question_patterns: the average harvest per tree is 25.6 but one tree is 3 too high - find the correct average for 15 trees

does an over-recorded value raise or lower the mean
recompute the mean after removing an erroneous reading

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the old mean by the number of values.
Subtract the recorded excess to get the true total.

concepts.title: Median and the Effect of New Values
concepts.definition: The median is the middle value of sorted data, or the average of the two middle values; adding a value larger than the median pushes the median up and a smaller value pulls it down, so the median of 8 becomes 9.5 when 11 joins and the middle pair turns into 8 and 11.
concepts.key_idea: Sort first: the median sits with equal numbers of values on each side.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp205.txt lines 80-105 (median behaviour with added values)
question_patterns: find the median of the given data set

compare how the mean and the median respond to a large value

solution_steps.explain: Arrange all values in increasing order.
For odd counts take the central value; for even counts average the two central ones.
A value above the middle raises the median, below lowers it.

concepts.title: Mean with Frequencies
concepts.definition: When values repeat, each value is weighted by how often it occurs: multiply every distinct value by its frequency, add these products, and divide by the total frequency - this is how an average family size is worked out from a frequency table.
concepts.key_idea: Frequency acts as a weight: bigger counts pull the mean toward their value.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp205.txt lines 200-240 (mean and median with frequencies)
question_patterns: find the average family size from a frequency table
calculate the mean of data given with frequencies
why is each value multiplied by its frequency before averaging
compute the weighted mean of two values with counts f1 and f2
how does the total frequency enter the average calculation
compare the frequency method with listing every repeated value

solution_steps.action: total each value times its frequency
solution_steps.explain: Weighted contributions add up to the overall total.
The mean is the weighted total over all observations.

concepts.title: Line Graphs and Interpreting Data
concepts.definition: A line graph joins data points recorded over time, making rises, falls and flat stretches easy to follow; reading one means first identifying the axes, scale and markers, then inferring trends such as Punjab's temperature peaking at 38 degrees in June while Kerala stays nearly flat.
concepts.key_idea: Two-step reading: identify what is plotted, then infer the trend over time.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp205.txt lines 678-760 (visualising data, line graphs, temperature)
question_patterns: read the monthly maximum temperature trend of Punjab from the line graph

solution_steps.explain: Note the axes, the scale, the time range and the markers used.
Follow rises, falls and flats for each data series.
Summarise peaks, dips and flat periods as conclusions about the data.

extracted_variables.count: number of values in the data

solution_template.explain: Mean times count recovers the full sum.

worked_examples.question_pattern: The average of {count} numbers is {mean}. Find their total sum.

solution_template.explain: The product is the total of all values.

worked_examples.question_pattern: The mean of {count} observations is {mean}, but one entry exceeds the truth by {error}. Find the correct total.

solution_template.explain: Mean times count gives the wrong total.
Subtract the error for the true total.

worked_examples.question_pattern: After correcting an entry, the true total is {correct_total} for {count} observations. Find the correct mean.

solution_template.explain: True total over count gives the corrected mean.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A frequency table has value {v1} occurring {f1} times and value {v2} occurring {f2} times. Find the mean.

solution_template.explain: Multiply each value by its frequency and add.
Mean equals weighted total over all observations.
